what: Cost of the durable commit token (domain-commit.token) on the default-config domain write path: the same working tree with the token I/O and without it. Three invocations of the same protocol; two are used, the third is kept and discarded because the host was taken over mid-run.

measuredSource.tokenOnSide: byte copy of this file, verified by the script before measuring
measuredSource.tokenOffSide: this file with writeCommitToken()'s file operations replaced by a no-op that still draws the same two commitTokenEntropy() values
measuredSource.note: Earlier revisions of this file (schema @1) measured abbc8df8c65e8f5ab5dc312575adb8c60bef91473bc83308aaa5c2d37f5d582e, an implementation whose token draw came from the stubbed crypto.randomUUID() sequence. That record is superseded: the numbers below are for the source digest above and nothing else.

protocol.workload: openDomainStorage over the official DomainFacility/JsonStorageBackend, then public port.observe() per write: stage mirror, memory load, work, commit, archive install, hydrate; fixture reset, assertions, snapshots and hashes are outside the timed interval
protocol.order: alternate tokenon/tokenoff per iteration; both sides run in the same fixture path; measured pairs are iterations 2-4
protocol.uuid: crypto.randomUUID replaced by a per-run deterministic sequence, counter reset before every run
protocol.entropy: commitTokenEntropy() is randomBytes(16).toString('hex'), which is not stubbed, so the token draw does not shift the record-id sequence on either side
protocol.compared: every persisted byte except domain-archive-lock and domain-commit.token, the query projections, the post-restart projections and the persisted shape; asserted for every pair (warmup included)
deviationFromPinnedHarness: The two sides are the same working tree with and without the token I/O, not release/dsh-evolution-0.2.0-rc.8.tgz vs the working tree. The pinned harness asserts every persisted byte is identical, which the token round cannot satisfy: the token adds a file to the compared tree.

domain-commit.token is excluded from the persisted-tree digest because it is the artifact under measurement; every other file, the query projections and the post-restart projections are still compared exactly. The exclusion is one path, not a mask over the rest of the tree.

diff: -  catch (error) { try { fs.unlinkSync(temporary); } catch {} throw error; }
tokenOffVariant.note: writeCommitToken keeps both commitTokenEntropy() draws so the two sides evaluate the same expression sequence and only the two file operations are removed. The script asserts the four replaced lines still occur exactly once in writeCommitToken() and exits non-zero otherwise, so a source drift cannot silently degrade this into 'token on vs a slightly different token on'.

tokenOperationsPerCommit.method: node:fs patched by path before the port module is materialized, then one live port.observe() per sample (five samples) over the same fixture as the A/B
tokenOperationsPerCommit.note: read=2, write=2 (each write is one temporary file plus one rename), unlink=0, and nothing at open; the count is steady from the first write. 4 commitTokenEntropy() draws per write, two per atomic replace.

runs.label: run-3-discarded
runs.invalidReason: the host was taken over by unrelated work during the run: load average 2.02 -> 53.00 (1-min 20.34 after the run), and the sessions under load 35.8-56.2 s wall against 33.8-36.9 s in run-1/run-2. Sessions 5-8 recovered, sessions 2-4 did not, so the run compares differently-loaded sessions and its summary reverses to -0.97% CPU. This is an environment defect, not a measurement of the token.

combined.note: the two valid runs disagree on whether the per-side ranges are disjoint: run-1 excludes 0, run-2 does not, because one session of run-2 (tokenoff, iteration 4) ran 39228 ms of wall clock against a 35497 ms run median while its own pair partner stayed normal. The pooled median over the six sessions per side is reported as the central estimate, and the per-pair spread is reported instead of a confidence interval.
